focuses.title: The Imperial Dawn
focuses.desc: A new century has brought the Empire to the edge of a struggle for the Pacific. Mobilize the government behind a common program and prepare the court to decide what the Rising Sun will become.

focuses.title: Convene the Imperial Court
focuses.desc: The Emperor, crown prince and military establishment command different sources of authority. Hear their immediate proposals and open a scheduled court review that can begin the succession debate without defeat or war.

focuses.title: The Divine Mandate
focuses.desc: Yoshiro's authority rests on the conviction that the dynasty embodies Japan's destiny. Reaffirm that bond before military setbacks and political rivals can turn public doubt into a crisis of legitimacy.

focuses.title: The Crown Prince
focuses.desc: Tatsu believes that scientific achievement can secure the Empire's future. Give the crown prince a public platform, open a channel to his technocratic allies and, if the intelligence service is ready, begin investigating the evidence behind the crisis.

focuses.title: The Emperor's Shadow
focuses.desc: Shinzo's officers have served the throne without receiving a voice equal to their power. Bring the military establishment into the court's deliberations, while recognizing that its ambitions may outgrow its loyalty.

focuses.title: Imperial Intelligence Bureau
focuses.desc: The court cannot answer threats it cannot see. Organize an Imperial intelligence service to uncover foreign secrets, detect hostile agents and investigate the evidence behind the growing political crisis.

focuses.title: The Question of Destiny
focuses.desc: A scheduled court review or an unfolding crisis has opened a public debate over Imperial government. Prepare the choice between Yoshiro's authority, Tatsu's technical administration and Shinzo's military command.

focuses.title: Reaffirm the Divine Mandate
focuses.desc: The throne need not wait for defeat to defend its authority. Reaffirm Yoshiro's rule, restore administrative confidence and choose how the court will settle its internal disputes.

focuses.title: Purge the Doubters
focuses.desc: Scientific skeptics and reformist advisors have challenged the foundations of Imperial rule. Remove their influence from the court, accepting the damage that a political purge will inflict on research and open debate.

focuses.title: Absolute Loyalty
focuses.desc: An army divided in its allegiance cannot carry out the Emperor's will. Bind its institutions more closely to the throne, strengthening discipline while narrowing the government's political freedom.

focuses.title: Reconcile the Court
focuses.desc: Moderate critics can serve the dynasty without surrendering all their convictions. Negotiate either a technical advisory settlement or a joint service compact, preserving Tatsu's eligibility as an advisor and commander.

focuses.title: The Emperor's Sacred Will
focuses.desc: Public loyalty must support practical national service. Deliver a one-time package of manpower and infantry equipment while reaffirming the Emperor's mandate and institutional legitimacy.

focuses.title: The Sacred Offensive
focuses.desc: The Emperor's supporters demand a decisive demonstration of strength. Prepare a period of concentrated offensive effort, accepting the additional supply burden that an ambitious advance will impose.

focuses.title: Warriors of Destiny
focuses.desc: Technology must serve the resolve of the soldiers who carry it into battle. Strengthen the infantry and special forces entrusted with the Emperor's offensive strategy.

focuses.title: Defend the Sacred Homeland
focuses.desc: The dynasty's first obligation is to preserve the country from which its authority flows. Concentrate the armed forces on the defense of Japan, even at the expense of operational mobility abroad.

focuses.title: Imperial Fortresses
focuses.desc: Defensive doctrine needs engineers, concrete and protected industry. Fund two construction grants in selected homeland industrial regions, reserving civilian capacity while fortifications and air defenses are prepared.

focuses.title: The Eternal Empire
focuses.desc: The throne has survived its challenge and chosen a lasting military direction. Consolidate Yoshiro's settlement into a state built around Imperial continuity and disciplined national service.

focuses.title: Tatsu Assumes Command
focuses.desc: The Empire's future cannot depend on inherited certainty alone. Entrust national leadership to Tatsu and begin replacing the old balance of court factions with government directed by scientific achievement.

focuses.title: Question the Old Order
focuses.desc: The institutions that secured Japan's rise may now be obstructing its progress. Permit a systematic challenge to inherited practices, gaining scientific freedom while disturbing the old political settlement.

focuses.title: Force the Emperor's Abdication
focuses.desc: A new program cannot advance while the old Emperor retains the final word. Compel Yoshiro to abdicate and place Tatsu on the throne, accepting the immediate instability of a forced succession.

focuses.title: A New Emperor
focuses.desc: Tatsu must establish authority as a ruler as well as an innovator. Build a government around the new Emperor's program while traditionalists organize against the manner of his accession.

focuses.title: Preserve the Emperor
focuses.desc: The throne can reassure traditionalists or participate in technical administration. Negotiate the terms of Yoshiro's preserved position, choosing ceremonial stability or a more ambitious scientific settlement with political risks.

focuses.title: Empower the Technocrats
focuses.desc: Engineers and researchers need authority over the institutions they are expected to transform. Give the technical ministries a coordinating role in production, procurement and the Empire's next generation of weapons.

focuses.title: Automated Warfare
focuses.desc: Automated industry supports armored production through cheaper equipment and faster technical development. Fund armored contracts to equip formations, while accepting additional steel and supply costs without a direct reduction in battalion manpower requirements.

focuses.title: Robotic Legions
focuses.desc: Experimental machines must become equipment that formations can maintain and deploy. Develop the industrial and technical base for mechanized forces and heavy robotic warfare.

focuses.title: Human-Machine Doctrine
focuses.desc: Technical superiority depends on trained troops as well as machines. Standardize mixed formations and authorize funded infantry and support-equipment contracts, strengthening the organization of a professional army.

focuses.title: Professional Armed Forces
focuses.desc: Advanced equipment cannot compensate for confused orders and poorly trained formations. Establish a professional force whose planning and operational experience match its technological resources.

focuses.title: The Empire of Tomorrow
focuses.desc: Tatsu's political and military reforms now form a coherent national program. Consolidate the technocratic settlement and turn scientific achievement into a durable source of authority.

focuses.title: The Military Conspiracy
focuses.desc: Shinzo believes the court can no longer defend Japan. Organize a military challenge to its authority; strong military influence may secure a peaceful transfer, while weak support risks an armed loyalist response.

focuses.title: Proclaim a National Emergency
focuses.desc: The military must present its intervention as an answer to an immediate national danger. Declare an emergency and rally support, accepting the instability created by suspending normal political restraints.

focuses.title: The Shogunate Coup
focuses.desc: Present the military ultimatum to the Imperial Court. Support within the armed forces determines whether Shinzo can negotiate a bloodless transfer or must confront an Imperial-loyalist rebellion; abandoning the attempt can restore Yoshiro.

focuses.title: The Bloodless Coup
focuses.desc: Enough of the establishment has accepted the new balance of power to make open fighting unnecessary. Complete the negotiated transfer and place the military government in command of the state.

focuses.title: March on Tokyo
focuses.desc: The court has refused to yield and loyalist officers are preparing resistance. Commit to an armed seizure of power, keeping Shinzo's government in EOR while an Imperial-loyalist faction takes up arms.

focuses.title: Crush the Loyalists
focuses.desc: The loyalist rebellion must be defeated before the new government can claim effective control. Finish the civil conflict and dismantle the armed opposition to Shinzo's rule.

focuses.title: Military Government
focuses.desc: The seizure of power must become a functioning administration. Consolidate the military government and place the surviving institutions of state under its authority.

focuses.title: Army Supremacy
focuses.desc: Continental campaigns require a government that gives the army first claim on strategic resources. Make land warfare the organizing priority of Shinzo's military settlement.

focuses.title: The Land Shogunate
focuses.desc: Shinzo's army commands must turn their political priority into sustained field readiness. Establish mobile logistics and authorize paid armored and support-equipment contracts with an operational preparation period.

focuses.title: Naval Supremacy
focuses.desc: The Empire's survival depends on the sea lanes between its scattered territories. Give the navy priority in strategic planning and the allocation of military resources.

focuses.title: The Oceanic Shogunate
focuses.desc: A naval government must keep ships serviceable between operations. Coordinate fleet protection and authorize funded shipyard, repair and readiness programs before the next maritime campaign.

focuses.title: The Supreme Shogunate
focuses.desc: The military settlement needs an agreed command above its competing services. Unite the institutions under Shinzo’s authority; a later major success can bring public recognition of the Supreme Shogun title.

focuses.title: Imperial Ambition
focuses.desc: The Empire's scattered commitments demand a strategic purpose. Bring its overseas ambitions before the government and begin planning the campaigns that would make them achievable.

focuses.title: The Imperial War Plan
focuses.desc: The armed services cannot pursue every objective at once. Establish a common war plan and choose the first theater to receive the Empire's concentrated effort.

focuses.title: Northern Thunder
focuses.desc: The Soviet Far East offers a continental challenge to Imperial power. Give the northern campaign priority as our first major strategic commitment.

focuses.title: Pacific Storm
focuses.desc: Allied sea power stands between the Empire and command of the Pacific. Make the oceanic struggle our first strategic priority and prepare its opening operations.

focuses.title: Consolidate Asia
focuses.desc: Regional security must precede a distant confrontation with the superpowers. Choose consolidation in Asia as the Empire's first major strategic commitment.

focuses.title: The Northern War Plan
focuses.desc: A northern campaign needs its own logistical and operational framework. Open the Soviet theater once it is our chosen priority or a later strategic reassessment permits expansion.

focuses.title: Operation Vorkuta
focuses.desc: Continental distances will punish any force that advances without preparation. Organize the northern offensive and establish the military foundations for operations against the Soviet Union.

focuses.title: Strike at Vladivostok
focuses.desc: Vladivostok anchors Soviet power on the Pacific coast. Prepare the attack on this first major objective and the prestige claim that will follow its capture.

focuses.title: Secure the Far East
focuses.desc: A captured port is only the beginning of a stable continental position. Consolidate the Far Eastern campaign and strengthen the forces that must hold its approaches.

focuses.title: Advance Through Siberia
focuses.desc: The advance now depends on surviving distance, weather and a thin transport network. Adapt our logistics to Siberia and prepare the next stage of the northern war.

focuses.title: The Odessa Operation
focuses.desc: An objective on a staff map does not supply an army. Authorize a prepared Soviet campaign operation combining offensive planning and urban combat support, timed by the player's operational decision.

focuses.title: March on Moscow
focuses.desc: Moscow is the political and military center of the Soviet war effort. Concentrate preparations for the final approach and make its capture an explicit campaign objective.

focuses.title: The Pacific War Plan
focuses.desc: A Pacific campaign requires secure bases and a coordinated fleet strategy. Open this theater once it is our first priority or a later reassessment permits it.

focuses.title: Fortify Pearl Harbor
focuses.desc: Hawaii is a vital forward base in the central Pacific. Strengthen Pearl Harbor's defenses and prepare it to support operations far from Japan.

focuses.title: The Black Tortoise Fortress
focuses.desc: A hardened Hawaiian base could absorb attacks that would cripple an exposed fleet. Develop the Black Tortoise defensive concept and authorize its costly preparation as a temporary strategic operation.

focuses.title: Challenge the Allied Fleet
focuses.desc: The Allied fleet must be confronted before our forces can operate freely across the ocean. Prepare the naval effort needed to contest its control of the Pacific.

focuses.title: Secure the Pacific
focuses.desc: Bases and fleet operations must support one another. Consolidate our Pacific position after preparing both Pearl Harbor and the challenge to Allied sea power.

focuses.title: Operation Santa Monica
focuses.desc: An attack across the Pacific depends on careful staging and sustained supply. Prepare Operation Santa Monica as the bridge from maritime control to a mainland campaign.

focuses.title: Assault the American Mainland
focuses.desc: The continental campaign must now turn preparations into a viable offensive. Establish the military basis for attacking the American mainland and pursuing its principal objectives.

focuses.title: Regional Policy
focuses.desc: Asia contains partners, dependencies and potential rivals whose interests cannot be reduced to a single war plan. Establish the framework for our regional policy.

focuses.title: The China Question
focuses.desc: China must decide how it will respond to the Empire. Prepare either a consensual partnership or a coercive approach, preserving the accepted borders until ordinary diplomacy or war changes the relationship.

focuses.title: Cooperate with China
focuses.gate: eor_diplomatic_cooperation_allowed = yes CHI = { eor_china_can_negotiate = yes NOT = { has_country_flag = EOR_china_partner } }
focuses.desc: Cooperation requires Chinese consent rather than an Imperial declaration. Offer partnership; Chinese willingness responds to relative strength, shared enemies and existing faction commitments, while additional economic terms require a separate Imperial agreement.

focuses.title: The Asian Accord
focuses.desc: An accord has substance only if China agrees to cooperate. Establish reciprocal industrial research exchanges with the current Chinese partner, while strengthening diplomatic confidence between the two governments.

focuses.title: Joint Military Plan
focuses.desc: Military access alone cannot coordinate two armies. Conduct joint staff exercises with the current Chinese partner, developing service experience and a temporary shared planning advantage.

focuses.title: Partners in Asia
focuses.desc: Independent partners need reciprocal arrangements suited to their relationship. Exchange limited electronics and armor research support with China, without admitting an independent country to the Imperial subject research group.

focuses.title: Subjugate China
focuses.desc: A continental campaign needs trained staff and specialist equipment before an ultimatum is delivered. Fund those preparations while accepting increased Imperial threat, then decide whether a refused demand should lead to ordinary war.

focuses.title: Imperial Ultimatum
focuses.gate: CHI = { exists = yes is_subject = no NOT = { is_in_faction_with = EOR } }
focuses.desc: Present China with the choice demanded by our policy of submission. Its government may accept dependency or refuse, in which case we must decide how to use the resulting war goal.

focuses.title: The Chinese Campaign
focuses.gate: CHI = { exists = yes is_subject = no } NOT = { is_in_faction_with = CHI }
focuses.desc: A rejected demand requires practical military preparation rather than another copy of a war goal. Prepare a temporary China-specific offensive, while bypassing this stage if diplomacy has already secured the subject relationship.

focuses.title: Imperial Protectorate
focuses.gate: OR = { CHI = { exists = yes is_subject_of = EOR capital_scope = { is_owned_by = CHI is_controlled_by = CHI industrial_complex < 20 } } AND = { NOT = { country_exists = CHI } any_owned_state = { is_core_of = CHI is_controlled_by = ROOT industrial_complex < 20 } } }
focuses.desc: A durable settlement needs industry and workable administration in territory actually controlled by its recipient. Build a civilian factory in the Chinese subject capital, or support reconstruction in an already owned Chinese core after annexation through normal war resolution.

focuses.title: Secure Southeast Asia
focuses.desc: The southern approaches link the Empire to essential bases and resources. Prepare a regional security program that strengthens our position in Southeast Asia.

focuses.title: Reinforce the Co-Prosperity Sphere
focuses.desc: The sphere's members need coordination if they are to support a common strategy. Reinforce the institutions and military preparations that bind the existing regional system together.

focuses.title: Asian Strategic Resources
focuses.desc: Regional influence is useful only if supplies can reach the factories and forces that need them. Improve access to the strategic resources on which an Asian campaign depends.

focuses.title: Establish Regional Supremacy
focuses.desc: Our regional preparations must produce a position that can survive external pressure. Consolidate the strategic advantages gained through the Asian program.

focuses.title: Global Reassessment
focuses.desc: The first campaign has revealed new opportunities or exposed the limits of our original plan. Review its results and authorize operations in additional theaters when the reassessment conditions are met.

focuses.title: The Second Front
focuses.desc: A wider war requires forces that can support simultaneous commitments. Organize the next front after the government has authorized a broader strategy.

focuses.title: Preemptive Strike Against the United States
focuses.desc: American intervention may become unavoidable as the war widens. Prepare an optional preemptive action, leaving the decision to declare war subject to the actual diplomatic situation.

focuses.title: Imperial Wartime Measures
focuses.desc: Military ambition requires an economy able to sustain it. Begin a coordinated industrial program that will settle the government's relationship with the zaibatsus and provide the foundation for mobilization.

focuses.title: Government-Zaibatsu Dialogue
focuses.desc: The industrial combines possess expertise the state cannot replace overnight. Convene negotiations to decide whether cooperation or direct control will govern the wartime economy.

focuses.title: Corporate Partnership
focuses.desc: The zaibatsus can expand production through their own networks and technical expertise. Choose a cooperative industrial settlement that preserves corporate initiative under national strategic direction.

focuses.title: Industrial Autonomy
focuses.desc: Corporate managers need room to organize production if partnership is to deliver results. Give the industrial combines greater operational autonomy within the agreed national program.

focuses.title: Corporate Innovation
focuses.desc: Independent industrial laboratories can turn procurement demands into new processes. Support corporate research and development as the next stage of the partnership economy.

focuses.title: The Zaibatsu Economy
focuses.desc: The cooperative settlement must become a complete industrial system. Consolidate the zaibatsu economy before extending it into a national mobilization framework.

focuses.title: State Control
focuses.desc: Strategic production cannot be left to bargaining among private interests. Choose direct state oversight of the zaibatsus and bring industrial priorities under government authority.

focuses.title: Imperial Planning
focuses.desc: State control requires a plan that factories can actually follow. Establish central production priorities and coordinate the allocation of industrial resources.

focuses.title: Nationalize Contracts
focuses.desc: Private procurement arrangements must conform to the state's industrial program. Reorganize strategic contracts and make their obligations enforceable through public authority.

focuses.title: The Imperial Arsenal
focuses.desc: Central planning must extend from legal authority to the operation of the combines. Complete their integration into the state-directed economy before introducing national mobilization measures.

focuses.title: Introduce the Imperial Mobilization Law
focuses.desc: The chosen industrial settlement now provides a framework for wartime coordination. Introduce a national mobilization law and authorize joint mobilization with current subjects.

focuses.title: First Amendment to Imperial Mobilization
focuses.desc: The first mobilization measures have exposed weaknesses in military procurement. Amend the law to support Imperial infantry purchases and a broader commitment to the war effort.

focuses.title: Second Amendment to Imperial Mobilization
focuses.desc: Sustained war requires production capacity as well as emergency orders. Extend the mobilization framework to authorize paid industrial expansion and maintain public support for the effort.

focuses.title: Imperial Resource Dependency
focuses.desc: Factories cannot meet their targets if fuel and raw materials remain uncertain. Establish a resource-security program, developing current Malayan rubber and Indonesian oil while the wider policy of autarky, supply or commerce is chosen elsewhere.

focuses.title: Synthetic Fuel
focuses.desc: Imported oil may be interrupted at the moment it is most needed. Invest in synthetic-fuel research as the first step toward greater domestic energy security.

focuses.title: Refinery Network
focuses.desc: Laboratory processes must be supported by practical refining capacity. Develop the infrastructure and expertise needed to sustain the synthetic-fuel program.

focuses.title: Resource Autarky
focuses.desc: Domestic substitutes can reduce the leverage of foreign suppliers. Consolidate a policy of resource self-sufficiency while accepting its industrial and commercial trade-offs.

focuses.title: Overseas Extraction
focuses.desc: The Empire's dependencies contain resources that domestic industry cannot easily replace. Make overseas extraction the central answer to our supply problem.

focuses.title: Resource Concessions
focuses.gate: OR = { MAL = { exists = yes is_subject_of = ROOT any_owned_state = { is_controlled_by = MAL } } INS = { exists = yes is_subject_of = ROOT any_owned_state = { is_controlled_by = INS } } }
focuses.desc: Resource concessions must produce material returns rather than another administrative permission. Add rubber in a controlled Malayan subject state and oil in a controlled Indonesian subject state, accepting higher overseas pressure.

focuses.title: Imperial Supply
focuses.desc: Extraction is only useful when resources reach Imperial factories. Consolidate the overseas supply system and the administrative arrangements that support it.

focuses.title: Open Trade
focuses.desc: Access to world markets may be more efficient than trying to produce everything at home. Choose commercial openness as the basis of resource security.

focuses.title: Commercial Access
focuses.desc: Trade policy needs reliable relationships with external suppliers. Improve commercial access so that industry can obtain the materials it cannot source domestically.

focuses.title: Maritime Commerce
focuses.desc: An open economy depends on shipping routes that remain usable in a crisis. Consolidate the maritime trading system while recognizing its exposure to naval disruption.

focuses.title: Ensure the Supremacy of Our Technology
focuses.desc: The Empire's numerical disadvantages make technical superiority essential. Establish a national research program to support advanced manufacturers, military reform and experimental science.

focuses.title: Approach the New High-Tech Companies
focuses.desc: New industrial firms possess capabilities beyond the traditional procurement establishment. Open negotiations with them and build the partnerships needed by the Imperial research program.

focuses.title: Kurikara Robotics
focuses.desc: Heavy robotic systems require specialists able to turn prototypes into reliable machines. Bring Kurikara Robotics into Imperial procurement and make its expertise available to the government.

focuses.title: Kanegawa Industries
focuses.desc: Armored warfare depends on dependable production as much as bold designs. Establish a procurement relationship with Kanegawa Industries and its armored-equipment specialists.

focuses.title: Shirada Shipworks
focuses.desc: A modern fleet needs shipyards capable of building and maintaining advanced hulls. Engage Shirada Shipworks as a central partner in Imperial naval development.

focuses.title: Tenzai Robotics
focuses.desc: Advanced aircraft demand close cooperation between airframe designers and robotic-control specialists. Bring Tenzai Robotics into the procurement network supporting our air forces.

focuses.title: Fund the Imperial Weaponry Institute
focuses.desc: Separate firms cannot answer every question raised by advanced weapons. Fund a central institute to coordinate military research, support technical ministries and provide a foundation for experimental programs.

focuses.title: Reform the Imperial Army
focuses.desc: The army must adapt its organization to the equipment now becoming available. Begin a common reform program before choosing the doctrine that will guide its specialized development.

focuses.title: The Futuristic Bushido
focuses.desc: The modern warrior must combine advanced weapons with disciplined individual service. Choose an infantry-centered doctrine that places elite troops at the heart of the army.

focuses.title: Imperial Warrior Armaments
focuses.desc: Modern infantry equipment must reach formations as well as drawing boards. Introduce Imperial Warrior production if necessary and deliver an initial equipment batch, even if the technology is already known.

focuses.title: Tankbuster Formations
focuses.desc: Enemy armor cannot be left solely to our heaviest machines. Organize infantry anti-tank specialists and improve the ability of foot soldiers to threaten armored formations.

focuses.title: Rocket Angel Corps
focuses.desc: Vertical mobility offers elite troops new ways to reach difficult objectives. Develop the airborne organization that represents Rocket Angel formations within our conventional forces.

focuses.title: Warriors of the Rising Sun
focuses.desc: The infantry program must become a coherent fighting tradition. Consolidate the training and equipment standards of the army's warrior formations.

focuses.title: A Highly Mechanized Army
focuses.desc: Machines can provide the mobility and protection needed for a decisive campaign. Choose a mechanized doctrine that organizes the army around armored and motorized formations.

focuses.title: Amphibious Armored Formations
focuses.desc: Amphibious formations require tanks that can be produced and maintained. Introduce Tsunami technology if necessary and deliver an initial equipment batch, preserving value when another program has already unlocked it.

focuses.title: The Tsunami Tank
focuses.desc: The armored program needs a vehicle suited to the Empire's operational environment. Develop the Tsunami Tank as a principal weapon of the mechanized force.

focuses.title: Heavy Robotic Warfare
focuses.desc: Some enemy positions demand firepower and protection beyond conventional armor. Extend the mechanized program into heavy robotic warfare.

focuses.title: The King Oni Program
focuses.desc: Heavy robotics must move from laboratory access into army service. Introduce King Oni technology if necessary and deliver a first equipment batch for immediate service.

focuses.title: The Shadow Warriors
focuses.desc: A smaller force can achieve disproportionate results through intelligence and precise action. Choose a doctrine centered on special operations, mobility and attacks against vulnerable targets.

focuses.title: Shinobi Intelligence Network
focuses.desc: Special operations require information before they require force. Build the intelligence network that will identify targets and support Shinobi-style operations.

focuses.title: Rapid Deployment Doctrine
focuses.desc: Opportunities disappear when specialist forces arrive too late. Improve deployment methods so that selected units can respond quickly to intelligence and battlefield openings.

focuses.title: Special Operations Command
focuses.desc: Scattered specialist units need a headquarters able to plan and sustain their missions. Establish a command structure for the army's special operations program.

focuses.title: Strike from the Shadows
focuses.desc: Special operations depend on command reserves and specialist equipment as well as doctrine. Supply support equipment and command capacity while strengthening the preparation of elite formations.

focuses.title: Landing Combat Scheme
focuses.desc: Every army doctrine needs a practical method for crossing defended shores. Develop shared landing procedures and amphibious equipment support as a common branch of army reform.

focuses.title: Multi-Terrain Combat Support
focuses.desc: A force that succeeds on the beach must still operate inland. Extend the common support program to reduce the logistical and environmental burdens of varied terrain.

focuses.title: Advanced Imperial Shipbuilding
focuses.desc: Shirada's expertise must be supported by a broader naval construction program. Develop the shipbuilding capacity and methods required by the next generation of Imperial vessels.

focuses.title: Imperial Naval Reform
focuses.desc: The navy must decide how to turn advanced hulls into effective maritime power. Begin a common reform program before choosing battleships, carriers or submarine warfare as its main emphasis.

focuses.title: Shogun Battlefleet
focuses.desc: Heavy surface ships can concentrate decisive firepower at sea and along hostile coasts. Choose a battlefleet doctrine centered on the Shogun battleship.

focuses.title: Advanced Naval Artillery
focuses.desc: A battlefleet is only as effective as its guns and fire-control systems. Develop the naval artillery expertise needed for heavy surface combat.

focuses.title: The Shogun Battleship Program
focuses.desc: Heavy naval construction requires sustained shipyard effort after a hull design is available. Grant the Shogun battleship technology, support normal dockyard production for six months and train naval staff.

focuses.title: The Fortified Fleet
focuses.desc: Capital ships must remain effective under sustained enemy pressure. Strengthen fleet protection, detection and repair practices before seeking a decisive engagement.

focuses.title: Decisive Naval Battle
focuses.desc: Heavy naval strength must be concentrated at the moment it can decide a campaign. Consolidate the battlefleet's doctrine for defeating an opposing fleet in a major engagement.

focuses.title: Carrier Fleet
focuses.desc: Aircraft can extend naval power beyond the reach of heavy guns. Choose a carrier-centered doctrine and organize the fleet around its embarked air groups.

focuses.title: Imperial Carrier Modernization
focuses.desc: Carrier operations depend on ships designed to sustain continuous flight activity. Modernize their equipment and operating practices to support the naval air program.

focuses.title: Tenzai Naval Aviation
focuses.desc: Naval aircraft must be developed alongside the ships and crews that operate them. Bring Tenzai's expertise into a coordinated program for fleet aviation.

focuses.title: Coastal Tengu Squadrons
focuses.desc: Land-based fighter squadrons can protect the fleet from nearby airfields. Deliver Tengu aircraft and train their crews, retaining the technology unlock as a fallback without promising carrier embarkation.

focuses.title: Air-Sea Battle Doctrine
focuses.desc: Carriers, aircraft and escorts must fight as a single system. Consolidate a doctrine that coordinates air strikes with the movement and protection of the fleet.

focuses.title: Submarine Warfare
focuses.desc: The enemy's supply system may be more vulnerable than its battlefleet. Choose a naval doctrine that places submarines and commerce disruption at its center.

focuses.title: Advanced Yari Submarines
focuses.desc: A submarine strategy needs crews and technology suited to sustained underwater operations. Develop the research and doctrine that represent the Yari program.

focuses.title: Torpedo Warfare Doctrine
focuses.desc: Submarines must make each attack count before the enemy can respond. Improve torpedo tactics and the operational methods supporting underwater warfare.

focuses.title: Disrupt Enemy Commerce
focuses.desc: The submarine force should threaten the movement of supplies across the ocean. Organize sustained attacks on enemy commerce and the shipping routes that sustain its war effort.

focuses.title: The Silent Pacific
focuses.desc: Submarines need trained staffs and safe maintenance cycles between patrols. Consolidate their defensive doctrine, gain naval experience and support fleet repair and withdrawal for six months.

focuses.title: Transformable Aircraft
focuses.desc: Tengu and Striker-VX development requires shared advanced airframes and control systems. Establish dedicated land-based fighter and ground-attack equipment; transformation and carrier embarkation are not represented by these aircraft.

focuses.title: Imperial Air Modernization
focuses.desc: Advanced aircraft need an air force organized to use them effectively. Begin a common modernization program and choose whether air superiority or battlefield support will receive doctrinal priority.

focuses.title: Air Superiority
focuses.desc: Our other forces cannot operate freely while hostile aircraft control the sky. Choose a fighter-centered doctrine that prioritizes winning the aerial contest.

focuses.title: The Mecha Tengu Program
focuses.desc: A fighter program should equip its pilots as well as support later research. Deliver twenty-four Tengu aircraft, train service personnel and retain a research bonus for conventional fighter development.

focuses.title: Advanced Fighters
focuses.desc: A successful fighter force must continue improving as enemy aircraft evolve. Extend the air-superiority program into the next generation of fighter development.

focuses.title: Dominate the Skies
focuses.desc: A mature fighter service needs reliable operations as well as agile aircraft. Upgrade the air-superiority doctrine into an integrated interception and mission-efficiency program, supported by temporary Tengu training.

focuses.title: Tactical Support
focuses.desc: Air power can decide a land battle by striking where the army needs it most. Choose a doctrine centered on close cooperation with ground forces.

focuses.title: Striker-VX Squadrons
focuses.desc: Ground-attack doctrine needs aircraft ready for ordinary wing deployment. Deliver twenty-four Striker-VX aircraft, train service personnel and retain research support for further close-air-support development.

focuses.title: Close Air Support
focuses.desc: Effective support depends on finding targets and coordinating attacks with friendly troops. Improve the methods that connect our ground-attack aircraft to the army's operations.

focuses.title: Support the Army
focuses.desc: Ground support succeeds when pilots and field formations share a practical doctrine. Upgrade the earlier tactical-support institution and fund a temporary Striker-VX training initiative for the air service.

focuses.title: Nanoconstruction
focuses.desc: The institute's research offers new methods for building and repairing infrastructure. Develop nanoconstruction and authorize paid projects that apply it in selected states.

focuses.title: Robotic Assembly
focuses.desc: Automation can extend from weapons to the factories that make them. Introduce robotic production methods to improve industrial output and production learning.

focuses.title: Establish the Nanotech Mainframe
focuses.desc: Research and robotic production need a common technical foundation. Connect the institute's programs through the mainframe and open the three primary experimental projects.

focuses.title: Liberate the Manpower
focuses.desc: Automation can release workers from tasks that machines can perform. Reorganize employment to make more manpower available, accepting the social disruption caused by rapid change.

focuses.title: Project Omega
focuses.desc: A single operative program requires focused scientific administration and specialized research. Establish those institutions now, then complete Yuriko's operational authorization before funding her individual missions.

focuses.title: Yuriko Omega
focuses.desc: Omega's results must be concentrated in a single trained operative rather than dispersed among ordinary formations. Authorize Yuriko's specialized missions, each requiring preparation and sharing a recovery period.

focuses.title: The Shogun Executioner Program
focuses.desc: Executioner research must improve ordinary procurement before a great machine is ready. Establish production-learning institutions and armor research support, then evaluate the prototype's operational reliability.

focuses.title: Authorize Executioner Preparation
focuses.desc: The prototype needs maintenance crews, supplies and a costly preparation effort. Authorize its construction as a ready asset, then activate the temporary Executioner operation separately when a war requires it.

focuses.title: The Giga Fortress Project
focuses.desc: Fortress research must support the fleet throughout development. Establish heavy-ship engineering and naval research support, then complete the prototype before paying for industrial preparation of a ready asset.

focuses.title: Authorize Fortress Preparation
focuses.desc: The fortress requires substantial industrial and logistical support. Authorize paid preparation into a ready asset, then activate its temporary national operation separately during war and accept the long recovery afterward.

focuses.title: Imperial Overseas Territories
focuses.desc: The Empire's overseas commitments need more than garrisons and declarations. Begin a common administrative and development program for the territories and dependencies that support its regional position.

focuses.title: Imperial Administration
focuses.desc: Overseas policy must have a clear institutional foundation. Review the administration before choosing direct Imperial control or a more autonomous cooperative settlement.

focuses.title: Imperial Centralization
focuses.desc: The centralized sphere will be held together by loyalty to the throne. Commit to stronger Imperial authority, accepting the administrative pressure created by deeper extraction and control.

focuses.title: Direct Imperial Rule
focuses.desc: Centralization requires officials able to enforce the government's decisions. Extend direct administrative oversight across the existing dependencies and strengthen the institutions of control.

focuses.title: Resource Mobilization
focuses.desc: A centralized administration can demand more coordinated access to strategic supplies. Organize the resource contribution of the sphere to support Imperial production.

focuses.title: Imperial Integration
focuses.desc: The centralized policy must become a durable administrative system. Consolidate its institutions before expanding the shared logistics and development program.

focuses.title: Imperial Partnership
focuses.desc: The sphere can endure through cooperation rather than unconditional obedience. Choose a partnership policy that increases autonomy and accepts limits on immediate Imperial extraction.

focuses.title: Regional Autonomy
focuses.desc: Local governments need practical authority if partnership is to be credible. Expand their administrative freedom within the cooperative regional settlement.

focuses.title: Joint Development
focuses.desc: Partners need a reason to see regional cooperation as a shared investment. Establish development arrangements that improve the sphere's economic and technical prospects.

focuses.title: Asian Cooperation
focuses.desc: Autonomy and joint investment must be supported by lasting institutions. Consolidate the cooperative settlement before extending the shared overseas infrastructure program.

focuses.title: Imperial Logistics Network
focuses.desc: Either administrative settlement depends on reliable movement between its members. Build a common logistics network after consolidating centralized integration or regional cooperation.

focuses.title: Develop the Imperial Oceanic Territories
focuses.desc: The Oceanic Territories need ports, industry and services connected to the regional logistics system. Authorize targeted investments that require the local government's continued subject relationship and control of its capital.

focuses.title: Technological Co-Development Initiative
focuses.desc: Infrastructure and joint development make a shared research program practical. Extend technical cooperation with participating dependencies while allowing its benefits to end when the relationship changes.

focuses.title: Imperial Global Expansion
focuses.desc: A wider campaign requires practical preparation across the armed services. Train army and naval staffs and support offensive logistics, while accepting that expansion increases the threat perceived by rival governments.

focuses.title: The World Grows Fearful
focuses.desc: Our growing power is giving otherwise hostile governments a common concern. Assess the danger that Imperial expansion will unite rivals against us.

focuses.title: The Coalition Crisis
focuses.desc: The international response now requires a deliberate strategic choice. Prepare to confront a coalition through a preemptive offensive, diplomatic division or sustained defense.

focuses.title: Strike First
focuses.desc: A coalition may be weakest before its members complete their preparations. Choose an offensive response intended to seize the initiative before their cooperation matures.

focuses.title: Preemptive War
focuses.desc: An early offensive requires clear objectives and preparations suited to the intended targets. Develop the operational basis for a preemptive war while retaining control over its actual declaration.

focuses.title: Crush the Coalition
focuses.desc: The offensive strategy must be capable of breaking organized resistance. Consolidate preparations for defeating the coalition rather than merely disrupting its formation.

focuses.title: Exploit Rivalries
focuses.desc: Our opponents' fear of the Empire does not erase their conflicting interests. Choose a diplomatic strategy aimed at widening those divisions.

focuses.title: Imperial Diplomacy
focuses.desc: Rivalries become useful only when supported by credible negotiations. Strengthen the diplomatic machinery required to pursue separate understandings, preparing a later eligible settlement request for 180 days without paying the request cost in advance.

focuses.title: Divide Our Enemies
focuses.desc: Individual agreements require work beyond opening diplomatic channels. Strengthen the Empire's diplomatic position, gaining political power and negotiating leverage against rivals while leaving every settlement request subject to the target's consent.

focuses.title: Fortify the Empire
focuses.desc: The Empire may survive a wider war by making its positions too costly to attack. Choose a defensive strategy built around protected bases and sustained resistance.

focuses.title: Total Defense
focuses.desc: A defensive strategy must organize industry and the armed services around endurance. Extend preparations from individual strongpoints to a national system of defense.

focuses.title: War of Attrition
focuses.desc: A long war will test supply, replacement and political resolve. Consolidate the preparations needed to exhaust an opposing coalition without abandoning the Empire's core positions.

focuses.title: Settle the Imperial Court
focuses.desc: The court needs a lasting division of responsibilities beneath Yoshiro’s throne. Consolidate the political settlement while the normal struggle between states continues.

focuses.title: Institutionalize Technical Government
focuses.desc: Tatsu’s modernization program needs institutions that can outlast a single project. Establish continuing technical administration as an ordinary policy of government.

focuses.title: Consolidate Military Administration
focuses.desc: Shinzo’s commands must translate military authority into everyday administration. Consolidate their responsibilities without prescribing how the wider war must end.
